input.content:
# PIPELINE — the z-image-turbo vertical slice

> **This file is rewritten, not appended.** It states where the pipeline is
> *now* and what happens next. History belongs in `TODO.md` (session
> handoffs) and `research/` (closed findings); if a paragraph here is about
> the past, it is in the wrong file. Keep it under ~150 lines.

**Status**: stages 1, 2, 3 and 4a done. A whole DiT block now runs on the GPU
— 26 dispatches, every matrix operation on the matrix cores — in **65.6 ms at
4096 tokens**, validated stage by stage against diffusers. That is **17.8 s
per image** for the transformer and **23.4 s** with the VAE, inside the
20-30 s this stage set out to accept. Next is stage 4b: the block's remaining
17% is elementwise passes doing no arithmetic, and one GEMM shape
(`dit.ff.w13`) is at 44% of the ceiling where every other is at 74%.
**Target**: `prompt → PNG` for Z-Image-Turbo at 1024x1024, 8 steps, fp16.

## Why this exists

Phase 1 — fifteen-plus sessions of microbenchmarks — ended 2026-09-13 with no
convergence criterion; `TODO.md` carries the argument. **The unit of work is
now "a thing that runs", not "an experiment":** a profiler chooses the
optimisation targets, the IDEAS backlog does not. Stage 4a is what that looks
like — it went looking for the kernel `results/shapes.csv` said would win and
found that the table's crown kernel is the *slowest* of five once the weight
can be stored the way the matrix cores want to read it.

## The model, as the checkpoint actually describes it

Read with `go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`. These differ
from `bench/modelshapes.go`, which was transcribed from `config.json` by
hand and has gaps that change the arithmetic:

| | |
|---|---|
| DiT blocks | **34**, not 30 — 30 `layers` + 2 `context_refiner` + 2 `noise_refiner` |
| Width / heads | dim 3840, 30 heads, head_dim 128, `qk_norm` on `[128]` |
| Attention | four matrices `to_q`/`to_k`/`to_v`/`to_out.0`, each `[3840, 3840]`, **no biases** |
| FFN | SwiGLU: `w1`,`w3` `[10240, 3840]` gate/up, `w2` `[3840, 10240]` down |
| Modulation | `adaLN_modulation` `[15360, 256]` + bias per layer; chunks are scale_msa, gate_msa, scale_mlp, gate_mlp, the scales offset by one and the gates through tanh |
| RoPE | 3D, `axes_dims [32, 48, 48]`, `axes_lens [1536, 512, 512]`, theta 256 |
| Latents | 16 channels, patch size 2 — 1024x1024 is 128x128 latents is **4096 tokens** |
| VAE | Flux `AutoencoderKL`: `block_out_channels [128,256,512,512]`, 2 layers/block, GroupNorm(32), SiLU, mid-block attention, 8x upsample, scale 0.3611, shift 0.1159 |
| Text encoder | Qwen3-4B: 36 layers, hidden 2560, FFN 9728, GQA 32q/8kv, head_dim 128, vocab 151936 |
| Scheduler | `FlowMatchEulerDiscrete`, shift 3.0, 1000 train timesteps, 8 NFE |

Sizes: transformer 6.155 B **F32** on disk (24.62 GB); text encoder 4.022 B
and VAE 0.084 B, both **BF16**. As fp16 the three total **20.5 GB**, so the
whole pipeline is resident in 128 GB unified memory at once.

## Stages

| # | Stage | State | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Checkpoint loader | **done** | `safetensors/`, `cmd/inspect` |
| 2a | VAE decoder, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/vae/`, validated stagewise against diffusers |
| 2b | VAE decoder, Vulkan | **done** | 10 shaders, 119 dispatches, 1024² in 5.6 s |
| 3a | DiT block, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/dit/`, validated stagewise incl. RoPE and qk-norm |
| 3b | Attention, Vulkan, scalar | **done** | 4 shaders; 1.28 TFLOP/s, kept as the oracle |
| 3c | Attention on WMMA | **done** | 38.8 TFLOP/s = 70% of ceiling, 30.4x |
| 4a | The block as a graph | **done** | `GPUBlock`, 26 dispatches, 65.6 ms; §2.8 (see below) |
| 4b | Fuse the tail, fix `ff.w13` | next | 12.1 ms of elementwise, and the one shape at 44% of ceiling |
| 4c | 34 blocks | | weight streaming: 12.3 GB of fp16 against a 4.29 GB buffer limit |
| 5 | Text encoder + tokenizer | | Qwen3-4B, GQA; BPE from `tokenizer/` |
| 6 | Scheduler + driver | | FlowMatchEuler, 8 steps; PNG out |

Each stage gets a CPU implementation in Go first: it separates "do I understand
the architecture" from "is the shader right", and once it matches diffusers it
is the oracle the GPU port is debugged against.

## The rule for every stage

Validate against the **diffusers reference**, not against a shape table.
`reference/dump_vae.py` and `reference/dump_dit_block.py` are the pattern:
run a fixed input through diffusers in fp32 on CPU, dump **every submodule's
output**, and have the Go test walk the graph stage by stage. Stage 4a needed
one addition to make that possible on a 26-dispatch graph — `GPUBlock.RunTo`
re-runs the graph's prefix up to a labelled dispatch, because most of a
block's intermediates are overwritten before it ends.

Every such test needs a **negative control** that deliberately breaks the
implementation and asserts the break is caught; without one the test proves
only that it runs. `zimage/vae`'s land 141x-14000x above tolerance, stage 3c's
27x-569x, stage 4a's **1160x-15828x**. Normalise the error by the tensor's
**RMS**, not per element — but know what that costs: two of stage 4a's stages
report 3e-2 where their worst element is 2e-3 of itself, because an RMS norm's
output inherits the learned weight's dynamic range.

## What the kernels already give us

Measured on this device (`research/`), and load-bearing for every stage:

- **fp16 is the fast path.** WMMA fp16 is 55.5 TFLOP/s; WMMA int8 is the
  *same* rate, not double (§0). The DiT's projections now reach **41.0, 74%
  of it** (§2.8).
- **Do not quantize the DiT for speed.** At M=4096 its intensity is `4*M` =
  16384 flop/byte against a 235 crossover, so it is compute-bound and 4-bit
  weights buy nothing (§3.4). Quantize for footprint only.
- **Coverage law** (§5.1b): achievable bandwidth is
  `min(1, C/gcd(stride, 4096))`, C being the contiguous run the in-flight
  requests hold. Land `gcd` in [128, 256] B. Getting this wrong costs 2-8x.
- **Store WMMA operands as 16x16 fragment tiles** — but *check* it per shape
  (§2.8). Free on a weight, since the packing happens once at upload; worth
  1.46x on two of the DiT's three GEMM shapes and a 5% loss on the third, and
  on that third one it makes §2.7's hoisted K-slab a 1.3-1.5x *loss*.
- **Kernel choice is per shape, and the table is stale the moment a layout
  changes.** `results/shapes.csv` picked `wmma_reg64_bt_hka4_padab128` for the
  DiT; measured in the real graph it is the slowest of five (24.5 s/image
  against 17.8).
- **Time dispatches, not `Apply`.** Reads out of the device-local
  host-visible arena run at **0.2 GB/s** (writes: 11.5), so any wall-clock
  figure that includes a read-back is measuring the read-back.

## Measured baseline to beat — the DiT block

`go run ./cmd/ditblock`, GPU timestamps per dispatch, best of three, two runs
agreeing to 0.994-1.006. Per image is 34 blocks x 8 steps.

| tokens | image | block | GEMMs | attention | elementwise | per image |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320 | — | 6.1 ms | 5.4 | 0.06 | 0.7 | 1.7 s |
| 1024 | 256² | 15.0 ms | 12.3 | 0.46 | 2.2 | 4.1 s |
| 4096 | **1024²** | **65.6 ms** | **46.9** | **6.7** | **12.1** | **17.8 s** |

TFLOP/s by shape at 4096, best build per shape (`research/stage-4-dit-graph.md`
has all five): `qkv`/`o` **41.0**, `ff.w2` **40.5**, `ff.w13` **24.3**.

## Measured baseline to beat — VAE

| latent | image | activations | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16² | 128² | 49 MB | 49 ms |
| 32² | 256² | 197 MB | 217 ms |
| 64² | 512² | 789 MB | 1.02 s |
| 128² | **1024²** | 3.16 GB | **5.6 s** |

Everything is fp32, and that wall clock includes a read-back. The next lever
is fp16 onto the WMMA path, which halves the arena and should move conv3x3
past its 3.3 TFLOP/s — stages 3c and 4a are now the evidence that fp16
operands with fp32 accumulators hold up when the intermediates are bounded.

## Where the image budget stands

| | per image, 1024², 8 steps |
|---|---|
| DiT, measured end to end | **17.8 s** |
| — of which projections | 12.8 s |
| — of which attention | 1.8 s |
| — of which elementwise | 3.3 s |
| VAE decode, measured | 5.6 s |
| **total** | **23.4 s** |

Stage 4b's levers, priced: fusing the norms into their consumers and the
q/k-norm + RoPE + pack chain into one kernel is ~1.0 s; an fp16 C out of
`w1`/`w3` (§2.6) halves both that GEMM's write and `swiglu`'s read; and
`ff.w13` at 24.3 TFLOP/s against its neighbours' 41 is worth 2.0 s on its own
if §2.4's swizzle closes it.

## What each stage found

Closed findings live in `research/`, not here:

- **[Stage 2 — the VAE decoder](research/stage-2-vae-decoder.md)**: fp16
  cannot hold this model's intermediates (1.16e7 against a 65504 limit),
  register-blocking beat every other conv fix 6.1x, §5.1b's coverage law
  predicted a 20x attention bug exactly, and two hard device limits — 4.29 GB
  per storage buffer, and a watchdog that kills a 5.5 s command buffer.
- **[Stage 3 — the DiT block and its attention](research/stage-3-dit-attention.md)**:
  the scalar path tops out an order of magnitude short and the matrix-core
  kernel reaches 70% of the WMMA ceiling — but only once every operand is
  stored as 16x16 fragment tiles. Three hazards a port hits: RoPE pairs
  *adjacent* components, the q/k norms are *per head*, and v is the operand
  that needs transposing.
- **[Stage 4a — the block as a graph](research/stage-4-dit-graph.md)**: 65.6
  ms/block; a fragment-tiled weight is 1.46x on two shapes and a loss on the
  third (§2.8), it interacts with §2.7's hoist, `results/shapes.csv`'s winner
  is the slowest of five in situ, and 18% of a block is elementwise passes.

# PIPELINE — the z-image-turbo vertical slice

> **This file is rewritten, not appended.** It states where the pipeline is
> *now* and what happens next. History belongs in `TODO.md` (session
> handoffs) and `research/` (closed findings); if a paragraph here is about
> the past, it is in the wrong file. Keep it under ~150 lines.

**Status**: stages 1, 2, 3 and 4a done. A whole DiT block now runs on the GPU
— 26 dispatches, every matrix operation on the matrix cores — in **65.6 ms at
4096 tokens**, validated stage by stage against diffusers. That is **17.8 s
per image** for the transformer and **23.4 s** with the VAE, inside the
20-30 s this stage set out to accept. Next is stage 4b: the block's remaining
17% is elementwise passes doing no arithmetic, and one GEMM shape
(`dit.ff.w13`) is at 44% of the ceiling where every other is at 74%.
**Target**: `prompt → PNG` for Z-Image-Turbo at 1024x1024, 8 steps, fp16.

## Why this exists

Phase 1 — fifteen-plus sessions of microbenchmarks — ended 2026-09-13 with no
convergence criterion; `TODO.md` carries the argument. **The unit of work is
now "a thing that runs", not "an experiment":** a profiler chooses the
optimisation targets, the IDEAS backlog does not. Stage 4a is what that looks
like — it went looking for the kernel `results/shapes.csv` said would win and
found that the table's crown kernel is the *slowest* of five once the weight
can be stored the way the matrix cores want to read it.

## The model, as the checkpoint actually describes it

Read with `go run ./cmd/inspect models/Z-Image-Turbo/<part>`. These differ
from `bench/modelshapes.go`, which was transcribed from `config.json` by
hand and has gaps that change the arithmetic:

| | |
|---|---|
| DiT blocks | **34**, not 30 — 30 `layers` + 2 `context_refiner` + 2 `noise_refiner` |
| Width / heads | dim 3840, 30 heads, head_dim 128, `qk_norm` on `[128]` |
| Attention | four matrices `to_q`/`to_k`/`to_v`/`to_out.0`, each `[3840, 3840]`, **no biases** |
| FFN | SwiGLU: `w1`,`w3` `[10240, 3840]` gate/up, `w2` `[3840, 10240]` down |
| Modulation | `adaLN_modulation` `[15360, 256]` + bias per layer; chunks are scale_msa, gate_msa, scale_mlp, gate_mlp, the scales offset by one and the gates through tanh |
| RoPE | 3D, `axes_dims [32, 48, 48]`, `axes_lens [1536, 512, 512]`, theta 256 |
| Latents | 16 channels, patch size 2 — 1024x1024 is 128x128 latents is **4096 tokens** |
| VAE | Flux `AutoencoderKL`: `block_out_channels [128,256,512,512]`, 2 layers/block, GroupNorm(32), SiLU, mid-block attention, 8x upsample, scale 0.3611, shift 0.1159 |
| Text encoder | Qwen3-4B: 36 layers, hidden 2560, FFN 9728, GQA 32q/8kv, head_dim 128, vocab 151936 |
| Scheduler | `FlowMatchEulerDiscrete`, shift 3.0, 1000 train timesteps, 8 NFE |

Sizes: transformer 6.155 B **F32** on disk (24.62 GB); text encoder 4.022 B
and VAE 0.084 B, both **BF16**. As fp16 the three total **20.5 GB**, so the
whole pipeline is resident in 128 GB unified memory at once.

## Stages

| # | Stage | State | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Checkpoint loader | **done** | `safetensors/`, `cmd/inspect` |
| 2a | VAE decoder, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/vae/`, validated stagewise against diffusers |
| 2b | VAE decoder, Vulkan | **done** | 10 shaders, 119 dispatches, 1024² in 5.6 s |
| 3a | DiT block, CPU reference | **done** | `zimage/dit/`, validated stagewise incl. RoPE and qk-norm |
| 3b | Attention, Vulkan, scalar | **done** | 4 shaders; 1.28 TFLOP/s, kept as the oracle |
| 3c | Attention on WMMA | **done** | 38.8 TFLOP/s = 70% of ceiling, 30.4x |
| 4a | The block as a graph | **done** | `GPUBlock`, 26 dispatches, 65.6 ms; §2.8 (see below) |
| 4b | Fuse the tail, fix `ff.w13` | next | 12.1 ms of elementwise, and the one shape at 44% of ceiling |
| 4c | 34 blocks | | weight streaming: 12.3 GB of fp16 against a 4.29 GB buffer limit |
| 5 | Text encoder + tokenizer | | Qwen3-4B, GQA; BPE from `tokenizer/` |
| 6 | Scheduler + driver | | FlowMatchEuler, 8 steps; PNG out |

Each stage gets a CPU implementation in Go first: it separates "do I understand
the architecture" from "is the shader right", and once it matches diffusers it
is the oracle the GPU port is debugged against.

## The rule for every stage

Validate against the **diffusers reference**, not against a shape table.
`reference/dump_vae.py` and `reference/dump_dit_block.py` are the pattern:
run a fixed input through diffusers in fp32 on CPU, dump **every submodule's
output**, and have the Go test walk the graph stage by stage. Stage 4a needed
one addition to make that possible on a 26-dispatch graph — `GPUBlock.RunTo`
re-runs the graph's prefix up to a labelled dispatch, because most of a
block's intermediates are overwritten before it ends.

Every such test needs a **negative control** that deliberately breaks the
implementation and asserts the break is caught; without one the test proves
only that it runs. `zimage/vae`'s land 141x-14000x above tolerance, stage 3c's
27x-569x, stage 4a's **1160x-15828x**. Normalise the error by the tensor's
**RMS**, not per element — but know what that costs: two of stage 4a's stages
report 3e-2 where their worst element is 2e-3 of itself, because an RMS norm's
output inherits the learned weight's dynamic range.

## What the kernels already give us

Measured on this device (`research/`), and load-bearing for every stage:

- **fp16 is the fast path.** WMMA fp16 is 55.5 TFLOP/s; WMMA int8 is the
  *same* rate, not double (§0). The DiT's projections now reach **41.0, 74%
  of it** (§2.8).
- **Do not quantize the DiT for speed.** At M=4096 its intensity is `4*M` =
  16384 flop/byte against a 235 crossover, so it is compute-bound and 4-bit
  weights buy nothing (§3.4). Quantize for footprint only.
- **Coverage law** (§5.1b): achievable bandwidth is
  `min(1, C/gcd(stride, 4096))`, C being the contiguous run the in-flight
  requests hold. Land `gcd` in [128, 256] B. Getting this wrong costs 2-8x.
- **Store WMMA operands as 16x16 fragment tiles** — but *check* it per shape
  (§2.8). Free on a weight, since the packing happens once at upload; worth
  1.46x on two of the DiT's three GEMM shapes and a 5% loss on the third, and
  on that third one it makes §2.7's hoisted K-slab a 1.3-1.5x *loss*.
- **Kernel choice is per shape, and the table is stale the moment a layout
  changes.** `results/shapes.csv` picked `wmma_reg64_bt_hka4_padab128` for the
  DiT; measured in the real graph it is the slowest of five (24.5 s/image
  against 17.8).
- **Time dispatches, not `Apply`.** Reads out of the device-local
  host-visible arena run at **0.2 GB/s** (writes: 11.5), so any wall-clock
  figure that includes a read-back is measuring the read-back.

## Measured baseline to beat — the DiT block

`go run ./cmd/ditblock`, GPU timestamps per dispatch, best of three, two runs
agreeing to 0.994-1.006. Per image is 34 blocks x 8 steps.

| tokens | image | block | GEMMs | attention | elementwise | per image |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 320 | — | 6.1 ms | 5.4 | 0.06 | 0.7 | 1.7 s |
| 1024 | 256² | 15.0 ms | 12.3 | 0.46 | 2.2 | 4.1 s |
| 4096 | **1024²** | **65.6 ms** | **46.9** | **6.7** | **12.1** | **17.8 s** |

TFLOP/s by shape at 4096, best build per shape (`research/stage-4-dit-graph.md`
has all five): `qkv`/`o` **41.0**, `ff.w2` **40.5**, `ff.w13` **24.3**.

## Measured baseline to beat — VAE

| latent | image | activations | wall |
|---|---|---|---|
| 16² | 128² | 49 MB | 49 ms |
| 32² | 256² | 197 MB | 217 ms |
| 64² | 512² | 789 MB | 1.02 s |
| 128² | **1024²** | 3.16 GB | **5.6 s** |

Everything is fp32, and that wall clock includes a read-back. The next lever
is fp16 onto the WMMA path, which halves the arena and should move conv3x3
past its 3.3 TFLOP/s — stages 3c and 4a are now the evidence that fp16
operands with fp32 accumulators hold up when the intermediates are bounded.

## Where the image budget stands

| | per image, 1024², 8 steps |
|---|---|
| DiT, measured end to end | **17.8 s** |
| — of which projections | 12.8 s |
| — of which attention | 1.8 s |
| — of which elementwise | 3.3 s |
| VAE decode, measured | 5.6 s |
| **total** | **23.4 s** |

Stage 4b's levers, priced: fusing the norms into their consumers and the
q/k-norm + RoPE + pack chain into one kernel is ~1.0 s; an fp16 C out of
`w1`/`w3` (§2.6) halves both that GEMM's write and `swiglu`'s read; and
`ff.w13` at 24.3 TFLOP/s against its neighbours' 41 is worth 2.0 s on its own
if §2.4's swizzle closes it.

## What each stage found

Closed findings live in `research/`, not here:

- **[Stage 2 — the VAE decoder](research/stage-2-vae-decoder.md)**: fp16
  cannot hold this model's intermediates (1.16e7 against a 65504 limit),
  register-blocking beat every other conv fix 6.1x, §5.1b's coverage law
  predicted a 20x attention bug exactly, and two hard device limits — 4.29 GB
  per storage buffer, and a watchdog that kills a 5.5 s command buffer.
- **[Stage 3 — the DiT block and its attention](research/stage-3-dit-attention.md)**:
  the scalar path tops out an order of magnitude short and the matrix-core
  kernel reaches 70% of the WMMA ceiling — but only once every operand is
  stored as 16x16 fragment tiles. Three hazards a port hits: RoPE pairs
  *adjacent* components, the q/k norms are *per head*, and v is the operand
  that needs transposing.
- **[Stage 4a — the block as a graph](research/stage-4-dit-graph.md)**: 65.6
  ms/block; a fragment-tiled weight is 1.46x on two shapes and a loss on the
  third (§2.8), it interacts with §2.7's hoist, `results/shapes.csv`'s winner
  is the slowest of five in situ, and 18% of a block is elementwise passes.

---
name: phase-2-pivot-to-pipeline
description: On 2026-09-13 the project pivoted from kernel microbenchmarking to building the z-image-turbo vertical slice end to end.
metadata:
  type: project
---

On 2026-09-13 Oliver chose to end the microbenchmark phase and build the
**z-image-turbo vertical slice** (loader → DiT → attention → VAE → PNG) with
real weights, accepting ~20-30 s/image at first. Image generation is the
priority model of the five in `GOALS.md`. Kernel work now continues only
where a profiler points, not where the IDEAS backlog points.

**Why:** after 15+ sessions, `bench/` was 84% of the Go code, every `api/`
endpoint returned `NotImplemented`, no checkpoint had ever been loaded (all
results were against random tensors), and the last iteration bought 1.09x
while attention and convolution sat at zero. The backlog generates new items
faster than it closes them, so it has no convergence criterion.

**How to apply:** prefer finishing a runnable stage over optimising a
measured one. Validate each stage against the diffusers reference rather
than a shape table — that is also what unblocks IDEAS §7 (accuracy), which
has zero work done and gates every format decision.

See [[strix-halo-bench-runs]] for how to run the old benchmark suite.

**Why:** the repo's TODO.md handoffs report a reproducibility figure for every
session (two runs of the family, median ratio and p10-p90 over common rows),
so a session that measures anything is expected to run its family twice and
quote the agreement.

to the scratchpad so run N-1 survives for the comparison, and check nothing
else is using the GPU (`/sys/class/drm/card1/device/gpu_busy_percent`) before
starting. Do not poll with `pgrep -f` — see

content.text:
Stage 4a is done: **the whole DiT block now runs on the GPU**, validated stagewise and profiled.

## What I built

| | |
|---|---|
| `zimage/dit/gpublock.go` | `GPUBlock` — one block as 26 dispatches over four arenas (fp32/fp16 × weights/activations), with a `GEMMPlan` that picks a kernel *per projection* and stages each weight in the layout that kernel reads |
| `shaders/dit_gemm.comp` | the projection GEMM — §2.7's winning arm on the DiT's binding/PC layout, with **three B layouts** as a build knob and five builds |
| 4 small shaders | `dit_adaln` (modulation + its four chunks), `dit_scale_f16`, `dit_swiglu_f16`, `dit_gate_add` |
| `cmd/ditblock` | times the block dispatch by dispatch and sweeps the ladder over the model's three shapes |

Plus `GPUBlock.RunTo(label)`, which re-runs the graph's prefix so a 26-dispatch graph can still be validated stage by stage; `vk.Buffer.WriteUint16At/ReadUint16At`; `safetensors.F32ToF16/F16ToF32` exported.

## Correctness

All thirteen stage boundaries the diffusers dump exposes, at 320 tokens: fp32 paths at 1e-6, projections at 1.2e-3, **block output at 1.7e-2** against an 8e-2 bound. Three negative controls land at 1160×/2828×/15828× the bound, and all five GEMM builds — three weight layouts, two tilings — agree to every digit. Full suite green (`go build`/`gofmt`/`go vet`/`go test ./...`).

## The measurement (two runs, agreeing to 0.994–1.006)

**65.6 ms per block at 4096 tokens → 17.8 s per image**, 23.4 s with the VAE — inside the 20–30 s target.

The finding is about where a weight lives. Stage 3c said fragment tiles *strictly dominate* the hoisted K-slab; on a GEMM's weight that is two thirds right:

| shape | natural B | tiled B | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `qkv`/`o` | 28.0 TFLOP/s | **41.0** (74% of ceiling) | 1.46× |
| `ff.w2` | 28.3 | **40.5** | 1.43× |
| `ff.w13` | **24.3** | 23.0 | 0.95× |

Two things I did not expect: `results/shapes.csv`'s crown kernel is the **slowest of five** in situ (24.5 s/image vs 17.8) — the table predates the tiled layout; and with a tiled B, *removing* §2.7's hoist is worth 1.3–1.5× on `w13`. Also, 18% of a block (12.1 ms) does no arithmetic at all.

Written up in `research/stage-4-dit-graph.md`; IDEAS gained §2.8, §3.3's claim is qualified, and §2.4/§2.6 gained the measurements that justify them. `PIPELINE.md` rewritten, `TODO.md` handoff added.

**Next (4b), in profile order:** `ff.w13` at 24.3 against its neighbours' 41 — it degrades with M and its weight is 157 MB against a 32 MB MALL, i.e. §2.4's swizzle, worth 2.9 s/image; the elementwise fusions (~1.0 s); §2.6's fp16 C. Nothing is committed — say the word and I'll commit it.

11	// fp16 arena, fp16 weights out of the weight arena, fp32 accumulators, fp32
12	// C back into the activation arena.
13	//
14	// This is gemm_wmma.comp's winning arm ported onto the DiT's binding and
15	// push-constant layout (dit_common.glsl), not a new kernel: same 16x16x16
16	// cooperative-matrix tiles, same WM x WN register-blocked accumulator grid
17	// (§2.1), same hoisted K-slab (§2.7), same padded leading dimensions (§2.3).
18	// What the benchmark kernel carries and this one does not is the machinery
19	// that made it an *ablation* -- the LDS arms that lost, the tile table of the
20	// grouped mode, its own four-buffer binding layout -- and what this one has
21	// and that one does not is the B layout the block actually wants, below.
22	// The two are kept apart deliberately: results/gemm_wmma.csv is a measured
23	// artifact of a kernel that should not move under it, and the epilogue
24	// fusions stage 4 will want (a fragment-tile C for the projections that feed
25	// attention) have no meaning in a benchmark.
26	//
27	// Three B layouts, selected at build time, because the model's three shapes
28	// did not agree on one in results/shapes.csv and the third is new:
29	//
30	//   B_LAYOUT 0  [N, ldb], K-contiguous, read with a column-major fragment
31	//     load. This is how a PyTorch `Linear` weight already sits in memory and
32	//     what §2.3/§2.7 ended on: the crown kernel at M=4096 on dit.qkv and
33	//     dit.ff.w2, 32.9 and 27.5 TFLOP/s.
34	//   B_LAYOUT 1  [K, ldb], N-contiguous, read with a row-major fragment load,
35	//     i.e. the weight stored transposed. Slower on two of the model's three
36	//     shapes and 1.66x *faster* on dit.ff.w13 (23.4 against 14.1), which is
37	//     the disagreement stage 4 inherited.
38	//   B_LAYOUT 2  16x16 fragment tiles: tile (nt, kt) is 512 contiguous bytes
39	//     holding element (k, n) at n*16 + k, tiles ordered kt-fastest. Stage 3c
40	//     found this worth 30x on attention, where a fragment load out of any
41	//     natural row stride covers 32 B of each of 16 rows and §5.1b prices it
42	//     at 32/gcd of the bus. The same argument applies to every B fragment
43	//     here -- and unlike attention, whose operands are activations that have
44	//     to be packed every step, a weight is packed once at upload and the
45	//     layout is free thereafter.
46	//
47	// The A operand is the same K-contiguous [M, lda] in all three: it is an

## What the kernels already give us

Measured on this device (`research/`), and load-bearing for every stage:

- **fp16 is the fast path.** WMMA fp16 is 55.5 TFLOP/s; WMMA int8 is the
  *same* rate, not double (§0). The DiT's projections now reach **41.0, 74%
  of it** (§2.8).
- **Do not quantize the DiT for speed.** At M=4096 its intensity is `4*M` =
  16384 flop/byte against a 235 crossover, so it is compute-bound and 4-bit
  weights buy nothing (§3.4). Quantize for footprint only.
- **Coverage law** (§5.1b): achievable bandwidth is
  `min(1, C/gcd(stride, 4096))`, C being the contiguous run the in-flight
  requests hold. Land `gcd` in [128, 256] B. Getting this wrong costs 2-8x.
- **Store WMMA operands as 16x16 fragment tiles** (§2.8). Free on a weight,
  since the packing happens once at upload. Worth 1.43-1.46x, and with §2.4 it
  wins every shape in the model.
- **Walk the grid in bands, not rows** (§2.4). `gl_WorkGroupID.x` fastest makes
  the resident workgroups a *row* of C, which streams all of B past one A slab;
  bands of 8 columns make it a tall block. Worth **1.84x** on the one shape
  wide enough to suffer — and only 1.16x if the weight is not also tiled, so
  layout and launch order are one lever, not two.
- **Kernel choice is per shape only while something else is wrong.** The DiT's
  three shapes disagreed on a kernel until both of the above were applied;
  then one kernel won all three at 73-76% of the ceiling. `results/shapes.csv`
  picked `wmma_reg64_bt_hka4_padab128`, which measures 23.5 s/image against
  13.4.
- **Time dispatches, not `Apply`.** Reads out of the device-local
  host-visible arena run at **0.2 GB/s** (writes: 11.5), so any wall-clock
  figure that includes a read-back is measuring the read-back.

## Measured baseline to beat — the DiT block

content.content:
## The rule for every stage

Validate against the **diffusers reference**, not against a shape table.
`reference/dump_vae.py` and `reference/dump_dit_block.py` are the pattern:
run a fixed input through diffusers in fp32 on CPU, dump **every submodule's
output**, and have the Go test walk the graph stage by stage. Stage 4a needed
one addition to make that possible on a 26-dispatch graph — `GPUBlock.RunTo`
re-runs the graph's prefix up to a labelled dispatch, because most of a
block's intermediates are overwritten before it ends.

Every such test needs a **negative control** that deliberately breaks the
implementation and asserts the break is caught; without one the test proves
only that it runs. `zimage/vae`'s land 141x-14000x above tolerance, stage 3c's
27x-569x, stage 4a's **1160x-15828x**. And when an optimisation *removes* a
stage boundary, keep the slow path and check the fast one against it: stage
4b's fusions are compared to the unfused graph at the last point their own
output is visible, where one of them is bit-identical and the other is 5.1e-4. Normalise the error by the tensor's
**RMS**, not per element — but know what that costs: two of stage 4a's stages
report 3e-2 where their worst element is 2e-3 of itself, because an RMS norm's
output inherits the learned weight's dynamic range.

## What the kernels already give us

## Measured baseline to beat — VAE

| latent | image | activations | wall |

| 16² | 128² | 49 MB | 49 ms |
| 32² | 256² | 197 MB | 217 ms |
| 64² | 512² | 789 MB | 1.02 s |
| 128² | **1024²** | 3.16 GB | **5.6 s** |

Everything is fp32, and that wall clock includes a read-back. The next lever
is fp16 onto the WMMA path, which halves the arena and should move conv3x3
past its 3.3 TFLOP/s — stages 3c and 4a are now the evidence that fp16
operands with fp32 accumulators hold up when the intermediates are bounded.

Stage 4b is done. Everything green: `gofmt`, `go vet`, `go generate`, full test suite.

## The result

**The DiT block: 65.6 ms → 49.3 ms** at 4096 tokens; **17.8 s → 13.4 s per image** (19.0 s with the VAE). The three GEMM shapes now sit at **42.0 / 41.1 / 40.6 TFLOP/s — 73-76% of the WMMA ceiling — on one kernel**, where 4a needed a per-shape plan and its worst shape was at 24.2.

| one change at a time, block at 4096 | block | per image | |
|---|---|---|---|
| `results/shapes.csv`'s pick (§2.7's crown) | 90.0 ms | 24.5 s | |
| + weight as 16×16 fragment tiles (§2.8) | 67.9 | 18.5 | 1.33× |
| + grid walked in bands of 8 columns (§2.4) | 54.5 | 14.8 | 1.25× |
| + elementwise tail fused, 26 dispatches → 18 | 49.9 | 13.6 | 1.09× |
| + fp16 C for the FFN's gate/up (§2.6) | **49.3** | **13.4** | 1.01× |

None of the first four rows changes the arithmetic — same flops, same tiles, same accumulators. Only the order of things moved.

## What the measurements said

**`ff.w13` was resisting the launch order, not the layout** — 24.2 → 41.1 TFLOP/s, **1.84×**. I derived the mechanism before writing the code and it predicted the measurement to within 10%: `w13` and `w2` have *identical* tile-level traffic (3.52 GB) yet realised 264 vs 439 GB/s, because X is the fastest axis and `w13`'s grid is 40 columns wide against `w2`'s 15 — so `w2` keeps four grid rows in flight and amortises each B slab four ways, `w13` keeps 1.6.

Three things I didn't expect: the optimum band is **interior** (2/4/8/16 → 36.0/39.2/**41.1**/38.3); the swizzle is worth 1.84× against a tiled weight but only 1.16× against a row-major one, so **ordering and layout are one lever, not two**; and per-shape kernel plans turned out to be a *symptom* — with both applied, one kernel wins everything and `DefaultGEMMPlan` is uniform again.

## Correctness

The fusions are checked against the unfused graph at the last point their own output is visible: the fp16 A operand is **bit-identical**, the attention context differs by 5.1e-4, the block by 1.6e-3 (bound 5e-3). The fp16 C is a precision trade, so it gets its own knob and its own measurement rather than being folded into the fusion claim — block error against diffusers 1.7e-2 → 1.8e-2, with `TestFFNIntermediatesFitFP16` as the range check (`w1`/`w3` peak at 250/508 against fp16's 65504; `w2` at 6e5, which is why it keeps fp32).

Two full sweeps agree to 0.998–1.020. IDEAS §2.4 and §2.6 are closed, §2.8 amended; `PIPELINE.md`, `TODO.md` and `research/stage-4-dit-graph.md` updated. I also corrected a figure I got wrong in the 4a write-up (a `w13` weight is 75 MB, not 157).

Next is 4c — 34 blocks, whose only new problem is 12.3 GB of fp16 weights against a 4.29 GB buffer limit. After that the largest remaining item in the image is the **VAE's 5.6 s**, 30% of the total with no optimisation pass yet. Still uncommitted.
